The question every leader lands on

How do you make AI as trusted and productive as your best people?

The answer

Give it the same knowledge and context — inside the same trust boundary.

Your best people aren't better because they're smarter. They know the business: who does what, what is happening right now, and where the good material lives. AI needs exactly the same — with the same permissions and controls your people already work under.

Part 1 · Under the hood

So what is Microsoft 365 Copilot?

One experience — four capabilities working together, all in natural language. Select a capability, or let it play — then compare answers with and without Work IQ.

or select a capabilityView as
Natural language
Enterprise data protectionCopilot Chat & Microsoft 365 Copilot
Ask in your own words|
Enterprise data protection — your data stays yours.

Signed in with a work account, Copilot Chat (Basic) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) are covered by enterprise data protection: prompts and responses get the same contractual commitments as your email in Exchange and files in SharePoint. Copilot runs inside the Microsoft 365 service boundary, honours permissions, sensitivity labels, retention and audit, and only surfaces what each person is already allowed to see.

Large language models

Copilot draws on frontier GPT models from OpenAI. By default it routes each prompt automatically — Auto, Quick response or Think deeper — so people get a fast answer or deeper reasoning without choosing a model themselves. Model names shown are examples from Microsoft's published model list; availability varies by Copilot experience and admin settings. Prompts, responses and work data accessed through Microsoft Graph aren't used to train the foundation models.

Your work · Work IQ

With Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium), Work IQ grounds answers in your work, within each person's existing permissions. Copilot Chat (Basic) works with the web and the files you attach.

“What should I prioritise before Thursday's EXCO?”

With a Premium licence, Copilot works fully inside Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OneNote. Depending on your licence, users without the add-on may have standard access in these apps. Part 1 · Trust by design

Built for a regulated industry

Copilot doesn't bypass your security — it rides on top of it. Here is what protects your data, and how a prompt flows.

Secure by design — Enterprise Data Protection

What Enterprise Data Protection gives youOn by default for anyone signed in with a work account — Copilot Chat (Basic) and Microsoft Copilot (Premium).
✓

Your data isn't used to train models. Prompts, responses and data accessed through Microsoft Graph aren't used to train the foundation models, including those used by Copilot.

✓

It inherits your existing protections. Copilot automatically inherits your organisation's Microsoft 365 security, compliance and privacy policies — including Microsoft Purview and sensitivity labels.

✓

It respects permissions. Copilot only surfaces content each person already has at least view access to — it never widens anyone's reach.

✓

Your data stays under your Microsoft 365 commitments. Prompts, retrieved data and responses are processed and stored under the same contractual commitments as your other Microsoft 365 content; stored interaction data is encrypted.

How a prompt flowsEvery step stays inside the Microsoft 365 service boundary.
  1. 1 · You prompt CopilotIn chat, or inside an app such as Word or Outlook.
  2. 2 · Grounding via Microsoft GraphRetrieves only content you're allowed to see — and/or the web.
  3. 3 · Large language modelProcesses the prompt in the Microsoft Cloud — not used for training.
  4. 4 · Responsible AI checksBlocks harmful content, detects protected material and prompt injection.
  5. 5 · Security, compliance & privacyYour Microsoft Purview and data-protection policies apply.
  6. 6 · Response back to youReturned in the app, with citations to its sources, for you to review.
Nothing new to configure. Copilot automatically inherits the security, compliance and privacy controls your organisation has already set in Microsoft 365.
Recommended before wider adoption: review content access (oversharing) in SharePoint and OneDrive, so sensitive information stays protected.

Source: Microsoft Learn — Data, Privacy, and Security for Microsoft Copilot; Application card: Microsoft Copilot (How Microsoft Copilot works); Enterprise data protection in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat; Data protection and auditing for Microsoft Copilot.

Part 1 · Beyond chat

Researcher or Analyst?

Two ready-made agents built by Microsoft — nothing to build, nothing to configure. The only decision is which one to brief.

✓ Built by Microsoft✓ Already included in your Microsoft 365 Copilot licence✓ Same data protection as Copilot
Ask yourselfIs the answer spread across many sources?→ Researcher
OrIs the answer hidden inside a file of numbers?→ Analyst

Researcher

Your strategy analyst. Hand it a question you can't answer in one search — it reads widely and comes back with a brief you could put in front of the Board.

Reaches for

The web and your work content — files, emails, meetings and chats you already have access to.

Trades

Speed for depth — it takes longer because it reasons in several steps.

Gives you back

A structured, source-cited report you can verify claim by claim.

Brief it when…
  • The cost of being wrong is high and you need to show your working.
  • The answer is spread across many sources: a market view, a partner or competitor picture, a decision brief.
Example prompt

“Brief me before Thursday's meeting with Bank Fabrikam: what public news says about them, what my emails and meetings say about the partnership this year, and a cited one-page view of opportunities and risks.”

ResearcherSource-cited
Planned the approachSearched the webRead your work contentDrafting the brief
Bank Fabrikam — partnership brief
web sourcesemailsmeetingsfiles

Tip: say where to look (your work, the web, or both) and answer its clarifying questions — that is how you steer it.

Analyst

Your data scientist. Hand it the spreadsheet — it works the numbers step by step, shows the analysis it ran, and tells you what the data is actually saying.

Reaches for

The file you give it — spreadsheets, exports and tables.

Trades

A formula for real analysis — trends, segments, outliers and forecasts.

Gives you back

Charts, tables and a plain-language read — with the code it ran, so your team can check it.

Brief it when…
  • The question is bigger than a formula: “what is really going on in these numbers?”
  • You want a what-if or forecast before a pricing, budget or portfolio decision.
Example prompt

“Take /Claims Data 2024–2026.xlsx and tell me what is really happening: claims ratio by quarter with a chart, the three products driving the change, any outliers or data-quality issues, and what to watch next quarter.”

AnalystRan Python · view code
Claims ratio by quarter
Q1
Q2
Q3
Q4

Q3 is the outlier. One large group-health claim landed in a single month — set it aside and the trend is steady.

Tip: hand it the file, not a description of the file. Clean, tabular data gives the best answers.

Which one would you brief?Five typical EXCO questions — make the call, then reveal.
“How are insurers in Southeast Asia using AI in claims — and where do we stand?”Reveal
ResearcherMany sources — the web plus your own documents — and you want a cited brief.
“Why did our claims ratio rise in Q3, and which products drive it?”Reveal
AnalystThe answer is inside a dataset; you want the trend, the drivers and the chart.
“If we reprice by 8%, does the loss ratio return to target?”Reveal
AnalystA what-if on your own numbers — you see the calculation, not just the answer.
“What should I know before meeting a prospective partner on Thursday?”Reveal
ResearcherPublic news plus your emails and meetings, pulled into one source-cited brief.
“Summarise this morning's emails from my direct reports.”Reveal
Copilot ChatQuick and everyday — no specialist needed. Save the agents for depth.
You'll see both today. Analyst live at 11:00 with the CFO — and you brief Researcher yourself at the start of the demo. Both come pre-pinned in Copilot for Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) users; more Microsoft-built agents sit in the Agent Store under Agents.

Both are built by Microsoft, run inside the Microsoft 365 data processing boundary and inherit the same security, privacy and compliance commitments; they respect your permissions. Treat results as a strong first draft — a person reviews high-stakes decisions. Example prompts and the illustrations use fictional data. Part 2 · Skill

The art and science of prompting

A good prompt has four ingredients — Goal, Context, Source and Expectations. Select an ingredient to isolate it, then build a real prompt one piece at a time and watch the request sharpen.

Simple prompt

“Summarise this month's claims report.”

A generic summary — no focus, audience or format.

Improved prompt
Basic
Click the ingredients above (or press 1–4) to build it
Goal

I'm chairing Thursday's EXCO meeting and need to understand why the health claims ratio is rising.

Context

The audience is the Board, who have seen the headline numbers — focus on causes and options.

Source

Use /October Claims & Customer Service Report and /October EXCO KPIs.

Expectation

Give me 5 key points, a cause-vs-impact table and 3 questions for the Head of Claims. One page maximum.

Keep the conversation going“Make it shorter — I need to read it out in 2 minutes.”“What did you assume? What should I verify?”

Leaders practise this in the executive hands-on. Source: Microsoft Support — Get started writing prompts in Microsoft Copilot.

Four use cases, the exact prompts

What each one does, the files behind it and the exact prompt — then your turn: the matching mission on your own work.

Watch ASSIST Copilot Workspaces
CEO

Your EXCO in one workspace

What it does: Create a workspace, add the four October reports and give it standing instructions — then ask for the decisions. Every answer comes from the same sources, with citations, and the context carries over to next month.

Contoso_Life_KPI_EXCO_Okt2026.xlsx 3 October reports (business · claims · programmes)
Workspace instructions

You are chief of staff to the CEO of PT Contoso Life Indonesia. Write for the EXCO: lead with the decision, use exact figures from the references and cite the source, flag anything that needs verification. One page maximum.

Prompt 1

What are the three decisions the EXCO needs to take in November? For each one: the figure behind it, its source, and the risk of waiting.

Prompt 2

Turn this into a one-page EXCO briefing: headline KPIs against target, the top three risks, and the decisions needed.

Your turnMission 01 Catch up in one minute→
Watch ASSIST Copilot Chat
COO

From meeting to follow-up

What it does: Copilot pulls the decisions and actions out of the meeting notes, then drafts each owner's follow-up — the COO reviews and sends them. In your organisation the source can be the Teams meeting recap itself.

Meeting notes: Weekly Operations – Claims & Service
Prompt 1

From the weekly operations meeting notes, what decisions were made? Show a table: decision, rationale, who proposed it.

Prompt 2

From the same notes, draft a short, polite follow-up email to each action owner with their task and due date. Show me each draft — I'll review and send them myself.

From numbers to foresight

Contoso_Life_Data_Klaim_2024-2026.xlsx (1,190 rows)
Prompt 1

Which regions drive the increase in health claims year-to-date versus last year? Separate the effect of claim count and average claim size.

Prompt 2

Project health claims and the health claims ratio for Q1 2027 by month, accounting for seasonality. Then test two what-if scenarios: medical inflation of 12% vs 15%, and an 8% repricing from March 2027. Show a comparison table and one chart, and explain the assumptions and limitations in plain language for the Board.

Part 3 · Your turn

Copilot on your own work

Five short missions on your own mail, meetings and files. Start Mission 00 first — Researcher works in the background — then try each mission right after its demo.

Mission 00Try1 min · Researcher

Delegate first

Brief Researcher now — it works in the background while you do the rest.

“Research how leading life insurers in Asia use AI in claims, underwriting and customer service. Give me a two-page brief with citations: real examples, the risks, and three questions our EXCO should discuss.”

Mission 01Try3 min

Catch up in one minute

Know what needs you before your first meeting.

“Catch me up on the last three days: the decisions I'm being asked to make, who is waiting on me, and anything urgent from my leadership team. Table, most urgent first.”

Tip: save this prompt to your prompts in Copilot Prompt Gallery and reuse it every Monday.

Mission 02Try4 min

Walk in prepared

Turn scattered emails, chats and meetings into a one-page brief.

“Prepare me for my next meeting on [topic or name]: its purpose, what was discussed last time, open items from my emails and chats, and three questions I should ask.”

Mission 03Try3 min

Pick one: sparring partner or read it for me

A · stress-test a decision before you take it to the Board. B · let Copilot in Word read a long document with you.

A · In Copilot Chat

“Continuing from that brief: I'm leaning towards [decision]. Act as a critical board member — give me the three strongest counter-arguments, what evidence would change your view, and your recommendation.”

B · In Word — open a long document you must read this week, then click Copilot

“Summarise this document for an executive in five bullets: the decision being asked, the key numbers, the risks, and anything missing or unclear. Then give me three questions to ask the author before I approve.”

Mission 04Try3 min

Read the research

Back to Researcher: open the brief and click two citations.

“Which three findings matter most for a life insurer in Indonesia, and what should we verify before acting on them?”

More prompts for your week

Copilot inside the apps you already use

Open the document, workbook, meeting or email first, then open Copilot in that app and paste.

Word

“Turn this document into a one-page summary for the EXCO with a clear recommendation and the three risks to watch.”

PowerPoint

“Create a five-slide presentation from /[file name] for the EXCO: the situation, the key numbers, the options, my recommendation and the next steps.”

Excel

“Analyse this table: show the three most important trends, one chart, and anything unusual I should ask about.”

Teams

“Recap this meeting: the decisions made, action items with owners and due dates, and the open questions.”

Outlook

“Turn this email thread into a one-page decision memo: background, what is being asked, the options, a recommendation, the risks, and the exact decision I need to make.”
